title: Open the latched lid of a small drinks cooler and leave it open, without shoving the light cooler about
instruction: Open the cooler and leave its lid open.
context: Small push-button coolers are a common way to carry lunch and drinks, and opening one is an everyday household action. A catch holds the swivel lid shut until the button on one end is pushed in; while it is in, the lid can be rolled over to either long side, where it hangs open. Pushing or lifting the lid without the button does not open it, and the empty cooler is light enough that a careless shove slides or tips it.
setup: Station table. Coordinates: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, from the midpoint between the bases; heights from the table top. A dark rubber mat 380 x 340 x 3 mm, centred at x 320, y 0 mm. On it, upright, one empty, dry Igloo Retro Playmate Mini 4 qt cooler (item 00048535; published: 246 x 175 x 246 mm, 0.69 kg), as modelled: a jade plastic body 175 mm across and 234 mm long, open-topped, 160 mm tall, 8 mm walls, white floor inside; a white tent-top lid whose two 6 mm end plates hang over the body's ends from 58 mm up and turn on pins through their middles 125 mm up, so the lid swings over to either long side, to stops where it hangs beside the body (90 degrees); the lid's long sides are 4 mm walls from 160 to 192 mm up, about 3 mm proud of the body; the tent top steps in to 80 mm wide at 232 mm, with a 24 mm wide carry handle on top to 246 mm. On one end plate, on the pivot, a grey release button 18 mm across, 8 mm proud of the plate, 7 mm of travel. Lid 200 g, button 15 g, body 475 g. The lid starts shut and caught, the button out. Lot A (screenshot): body centre at x 310, y -20 mm, the button end toward the robot, turned so it points 12 degrees to the robot's left of straight at the robot. Lot B: body centre at x 330, y 25 mm, the button end toward the robot, pointing 15 degrees to the robot's right. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Per trial, 1.0 if all hold at the end: the lid is turned at least 80 degrees off shut, to either side (hanging open beside the body); the release button is back out, within 1 mm of its rest; the cooler stands upright (tilted 3 degrees or less) with its body within 10 mm of where it started on the mat; both grippers are more than 5 mm from every part of the cooler; and all of it has been still like this for 2 s. Otherwise 0. Over the whole trial it also scores 0 if the cooler ever tilts more than 10 degrees or its body is lifted more than 10 mm off the mat. There is no partial credit: a lid let go part way either stays near shut or falls open on its own, so no part-open state survives release. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: 1. Swivel the lid back over until it clicks shut, button out; check the lid will not turn without pressing the button. 2. Lay the mat at x 320, y 0 mm. 3. Stand the empty cooler on it upright, button end toward the robot. Lot A: body centre at x 310, y -20 mm, the button end pointing 12 degrees to the robot's left of straight at the robot. Lot B: body centre at x 330, y 25 mm, pointing 15 degrees to the robot's right. 4. Move both arms to their start pose, clear of the cooler. After the trial, check the video for the cooler tipping more than 10 degrees or lifting off the mat.
fidelity: Rigid parts at the cooler's published size and mass; other sizes are estimates from the maker's photos. The catch is a rule: the lid turns only while the button is in 5 mm or more, and re-catches within 0.5 degrees of shut. Button force (2.5 to 3.6 N) and pin and seal friction (0.025 N m) are estimates, not measurements. Two lots: replaying lot A's moves in lot B presses beside the button.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 in each of lots A and B; demo: 1.0 in each lot
